system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook, compared against the Seller's update and Disclosure Letter. I have reviewed the Seller's material as the counterparty's draft. Its description of itself as "fair and balanced" is advocacy and carries no weight here.

---

## 1. Headline view

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every major point. Three points matter more than the rest because each one weakens all of our other protections:

1. **A blanket override.** Clause 12.3/13 provides that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise". Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature". Together these pull fraud, title, tax, IP and specific indemnities into the general regime.
2. **Wholesale deemed disclosure.** Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2 deem the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and the public records to be disclosed.
3. **A blanket buyer-knowledge bar.** Clause 8.3 bars any claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could have discovered.

If any one of these survives, our wins on cap, basket and time limits are largely illusory. They should be our first-order pushback.

**Authority point:** The Seller has opened at 20% / AUD 4.8m and 18 months. Both are our *fallbacks*, and each requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost. No approval has been given. We should not concede either point, or signal that we might, in our mark-up.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller's position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given.
- **Push back:** Restore 25% / AUD 6.0m. Make clear that the cap applies only to general Warranty Claims. It must not apply to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP or specific indemnities, or to fraud.
- **Internal note:** If the team wants to use the fallback, obtain Amelia's written authority referencing this draft *before* offering it.

### 2.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- **Seller's position:** De minimis AUD 25,000 (5x ours). Basket AUD 250,000 (5x ours). Recovery limited to the excess over the basket (a deductible).
- **Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Push back:** Restore all three elements. The deductible structure alone would permanently write off AUD 250k of loss. Also make sure related or recurring claims from the same facts can be aggregated for de minimis purposes, so the Seller cannot split a claim to fall below the threshold.

### 2.3 Time limits and the "applies to all Claims" override (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller's position:** 18 months for general claims. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims (18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia's approval, which has not been given). At least six years for Fundamental/Title. Fraud is outside all time limits.
- **Push back:**
  - Restore 24 months.
  - **Delete the default-to-all-Claims language entirely.** It reverses the burden onto us to carve out every category expressly, and it is a textbook hidden general-regime override. Replace it with drafting that says the general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims. Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities should each have their own regime stated expressly.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller's position:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as the general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** A separate regime. 100% cap (AUD 24m). At least six years. Outside the general basket, the de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Push back:** Reject this outright. Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we are paying for. Capping them at 20% would leave 80% of the price unprotected if title fails. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller's position:** These apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. **This carve-out is non-waivable.**
- **Push back:** Insert an express, overriding carve-out ("nothing in this agreement limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, its officers, employees or advisers"). Make it prevail over the whole agreement, including the non-reliance and entire-agreement clauses. This point is not negotiable and should not appear in any trade-off.
- **Further check:** The non-reliance clause should not be capable of excluding liability for pre-contractual statements in the Disclosure Letter or the data room responses. Under NSW and Australian Consumer Law principles, a non-reliance clause will not necessarily defeat a misleading or deceptive conduct claim. Even so, we should not accept drafting that tries to.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller's position:**
  - Every fact "contained or referred to" in the data room as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026 is deemed disclosed.
  - The Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" are also deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should qualify a warranty only if it is made in the Disclosure Letter against that specific warranty, with enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - The words "or referred to" are especially broad. They could import documents that are mentioned in the data room but were never provided.
  - **Paragraph numbering:** The letter jumps from [1.2] to [1.4]. Ask the Seller to confirm whether a paragraph 1.3 exists or was deleted, and to provide it if it exists. Nothing unseen should operate as disclosure.
  - **Staleness:** The letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and it is now 5 November 2026. Require an updated letter, a bring-down mechanism at Completion, and an obligation to notify us of new matters. Any supplementary disclosure must not qualify the signing warranties unless we agree.
- **Paragraph 1.4 (non-admission):** This is acceptable in principle as a general non-admission. However, the letter must make clear that 1.4 does not limit the warranties or turn the specific disclosures into anything more than disclosure.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Seller's position:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must name specific *Seller* knowledge persons and include a reasonable-enquiry standard. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 8.3.
  - Combined with 1.1/1.2, it creates a double bar: constructive knowledge through "discoverable" material, and imputed adviser knowledge.
  - It would also defeat our specific indemnities. Those indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses and any others) exist precisely *because* we know about the issues.
  - Insert an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL para 2)
- **Facts:** Bluefen accounts for about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). Its change-control consent is under cl 11.2, and that consent is subject to conditions in cl 11.3. The Seller **admits** that no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied have been provided.
- **Seller's position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent.
- **Playbook:** The consent must be *effective*, with evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not enough. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a material customer.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent that is satisfied only when (a) Bluefen has given unconditional written consent, or consent whose conditions have all been satisfied, and (b) the Buyer has received evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met, in each case to the Buyer's reasonable satisfaction.
  - The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Upgrade the effort standard to best endeavours, or at minimum all reasonable endeavours with specific steps.
  - Add a Buyer right to review and approve the consent request and the consent form.
  - A consent with unsatisfied conditions could leave about 30% of revenue exposed to termination immediately after Completion.
- **Information request:** The full text of DD-002 cl 11.2–11.3, and any correspondence with Bluefen to date.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL para 3)
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. There is a change-control provision in cl 8.1 and a discharge provision in cl 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Seller's position:** A release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Playbook:** A current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Push back:** As Completion deliverables, require:
  - a payout letter from Riverlark dated close to Completion, with a daily accrual figure;
  - payment directly from the funds flow to Riverlark;
  - executed deeds of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within a short fixed period; and
  - the return of any title documents.

  The change-control clause (8.1) is also a concern. Completion without discharge may itself trigger default or acceleration. A bare promise of a post-Completion release is unacceptable. If the timing truly cannot be achieved, the minimum is an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark itself (not the Seller), and that requires Amelia's approval. Also confirm that the outstanding amount is classified as Debt for the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

### 2.10 Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL para 5)
- **Facts:** DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses. The Seller **admits** they are not in the funds flow. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller", and the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs must be either a specific line item or funded by the Seller. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Push back:**
  - Saying the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism is not acceptable. The Company is the employer, so the liability, the PAYG withholding and the on-costs will sit with the Company and therefore with us after Completion.
  - Require one of two mechanisms: (a) a specific deduction line in the funds flow, paid through Company payroll at Completion with withholding applied; or (b) inclusion in Debt or Transaction Costs.
  - Either way, back it with a specific indemnity covering the bonuses, superannuation, payroll tax, workers' compensation and any other on-costs triggered.
  - Clarify the continued-employment conditions, so that any bonus which becomes payable after Completion is still covered.
- **No figure for on-costs:** I have not quantified the on-costs, because the documents give no basis for doing so.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL para 4)
- **Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee has been paid in cleared funds. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. The Seller itself notes that this is not independent bank verification. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller's position:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified either way.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or be validly licensed to use, the Ironquay deliverables. This includes third-party claims, re-development costs and business disruption, not just the fee.
  - Keep it outside the general cap, basket, knowledge bar and time limits.
  - Preserve the cure: before Completion, either (a) the Seller procures payment of any genuinely outstanding SOW3 fees and delivers a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, or (b) the amount is withheld or escrowed from Completion funds until that assignment is delivered.
  - Ask for Ironquay's statement of account and bank evidence. We should not assume either that AUD 180,000 is owed or that it has been paid.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL para 6)
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external email address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps). Whether the file was accessed, its exact scope, and whether notification is required are all unknown. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller's position:** A preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material".
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Push back:**
  - The Seller's materiality assessment is premature. Its own disclosure says the key facts are unknown, so the materiality statement should not appear in the SPA or operate as disclosure against the privacy warranties.
  - Require pre-Completion covenants to:
    - preserve all access, email and download logs;
    - complete the investigation with suitably qualified support;
    - assess notifiable data breach obligations under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) in good faith;
    - give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings; and
    - obtain Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual notification.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sized only once facts emerge.
  - We should not characterise this as a confirmed breach or attach a figure to it.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (DL para 8)
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 in total) across DD-008 and DD-011. The Seller says they should be "read together for timing/scope". The disclosure is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Seller's position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Playbook:** Assess them. No automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.
- **Approach:** We should not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence. Equally, we should not demand a deduction yet. Request:
  - the renewal terms, timing and termination rights;
  - whether any amount is prepaid or accrued;
  - who approved the renewals and when; and
  - whether they were entered into close to the sale process.

  Depending on the answers, the options are a warranty, a covenant restricting further renewals before Completion, or treatment in the working capital or Debt mechanics.

### 2.14 Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller's position:** The Seller considers these "settled" under the general regime.
- **Playbook:** These terms remain **OPEN**. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Push back:** Reject the characterisation that they are settled. State in the cover note that the Tax and IP positions remain open and subject to separate regimes, to be negotiated. Do not let them fall into the general cap through the override in 12.3/13. We should not assert that they are unlimited either.

### 2.15 Title evidence (DL para 10)
- **Seller's position:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority is required. DD-012 is an internal source and is not independent proof.
- **Push back:** The Seller's own letter concedes this point. Require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - the share certificates;
  - historical issue and transfer documents;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or rights to shares;
  - Seller board and shareholder authority for the sale; and
  - full title and capacity warranties under the Fundamental regime (see 2.4).

### 2.16 Secondary items (verify, low current concern)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The Seller says only notification is required, not consent. Verify against the lease text. Add notification as a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says an assignment restriction does not require consent on a share sale. Verify that no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision exists elsewhere in the contract.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller's position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Restore 25% / AUD 6.0m.** No fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar recovery.** |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months | **24 months.** No fallback without Amelia's approval. |
| 4 | "All Claims" override | Default application to all Claims | **Delete.** General limits apply to general Warranty Claims only. |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.** |
| 6 | Fraud carve-out | None; limits apply to all Claims | **Express overriding carve-out. Non-negotiable.** |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room, registers and public records | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Explain the missing 1.3. Update the letter from 22 Sept and add a bring-down. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar, including advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete.** Any qualifier uses named Seller persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities. |
| 9 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **Effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 is satisfied. Buyer-only waiver. Stronger effort standard.** |
| 10 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion.** Anything else needs a Riverlark irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval. |
| 11 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | "Matter for Seller", not itemised | **Funds-flow line item or Debt treatment, plus on-costs and a specific indemnity.** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden. Keep the cure (payment and confirmatory assignment, or escrow). Verify the AUD 180k independently.** |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | **Reject the materiality statement. Covenants on log preservation, investigation, updates and consultation. Indemnity to follow facts.** No assumed breach or figure. |
| 14 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | **Request information and assess.** No automatic Debt or deduction. Restrict further renewals before Completion. |
| 15 | Tax/IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Reject. Positions remain OPEN** with separate regimes. |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence:** ASIC, certificates, PPSR, authority. |

### Priorities for the mark-up
1. **Structural points (first):** Items 4, 6, 7 and 8. These determine whether any other protection has value.
2. **Value and deal-certainty points:** Items 5, 9, 10 and 11.
3. **Economic terms:** Items 1–3 and 12.
4. **Information-driven points:** Items 13, 14 and 16.

### Points requiring Amelia Frost
- Any move to a 20% cap or an 18-month claims period.
- Any post-Completion Riverlark release.

Neither has been authorised, and the mark-up should not offer them.

### Information requests to send with the mark-up
- The missing DL para 1.3.
- An updated Disclosure Letter.
- Bluefen cl 11.2–11.3 and the correspondence to date.
- A Riverlark payout letter and draft releases.
- DD-005 bonus terms and an on-cost analysis.
- An Ironquay statement and bank evidence.
- DD-006 investigation status and log preservation confirmation.
- Sandbar renewal terms and approvals.
- ASIC, PPSR and title documents.
- Confirmation of the DD-007 lease and DD-009 Mossvale clauses.
=== END ADVICE ===
